title: Verify drain follows plan order and stops at job boundary; fix gaps
summary: The repository already has plan-ordered drain (`prepare`/`Plan::build`) and `athena drain-stop` with `Stop::Requested`. I read the request as asking that these hold end to end: a newer, higher-priority request runs before older ones, and a stop request ends the drain between jobs without killing one. The job fixes any gap found and adds tests for it. The audience is the owner running `athena drain`.

defaults_applied.how: Tests added; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria check ordering and stop behaviour by running tests, not that code exists.
The producer fixes the ordering/stop gap itself, not one instance.
One focused change to drain ordering and stop.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
Recovered from drain.rs, README and the CHANGELOG that most of the request is already implemented.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs already orders work by plan (higher rung first, dependency, then age) and checks Steps::stop_requested before every job, per my reading of the file. The request text may predate that code.

The remaining gap is unknown. The most likely ones are an item with no plan entry keeping its place ahead of planned items, so a newer high-priority request cannot go first; the stop check not covering the approve/prepare phases; and the owner-facing docs. The producer should find these by testing.
The 'plan's priorities' means the requirements-ladder rung in athena_core::plan, not a new priority field.
No change to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows is needed.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`: a test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs queues an older low-rung request and a newer higher-rung request and asserts that the newer one is read and run first.

Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`: a test asserts that when a stop is requested during job 1, job 1 is finished, landed and rated, no second job is read or run, the report stop is `Stop::Requested`, and the remaining items stay in `queued`.
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass.

README.md, CHANGELOG.md and the drain.rs module doc state that queue order follows the plan and that `athena drain-stop` ends a drain only at a job boundary. The owner can read how to stop a drain without killing it.

out_of_scope: Moving compute to CI (the owner addendum itself)
Running jobs in parallel; the loop stays one job at a time
Changing the budget, retry or rating rules of drain
departures: The repository already contains plan-ordered drain and drain-stop, so the change may be small or tests only. Reading acceptance is lower because the real gap is uncertain.
